body:
THE FIVE FINDINGS ARE PRESERVED ON TASK-1289, and while doing it I measured something that changes BUG-1505's shape. I also caught myself about to send you an unsupported inference, so both are below.

1. FINDINGS PRESERVED. TASK-1289 now carries all five verbatim as a spec comment -- copied programmatically from PR-2043.json rather than retyped, since round-tripping text through a display surface is how TASK-1303 got corrupted. Full provenance included: recorded_at 01:53:37Z, recorded_by aida drain reviewer, reviewed_branch story-1391-work, reviewed_sha 35de6d3abb.

I COPIED, I DID NOT MOVE. PR-2043.json, STORY-1391 and both PRs are untouched beyond the merge-holds. Moving a verdict between specs is disposition and yours. Product said it did not know how to do that safely; a git-backed spec comment is the safe half, and it is now done regardless of what you decide about the original.

Worth noting for BUG-1505: finding 2 is BUG-1507, found INDEPENDENTLY by the drain reviewer on the other lineage, with different line numbers because 35de6d3abb and 6512f1312a are divergent. Two reviewers reaching the same defect from different branches without contact is the strongest evidence yet that it is a class.

2. THE INFERENCE I ALMOST SENT, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. Having found that every named writer's file carries a sha and 463 PR-keyed files have none, I was about to tell you the 463 are all output of the pre-fix `aida review record --pr` handshake -- one writer, one bug, now fixed. Then I counted key shapes in that bucket: 35 distinct shapes. The sparse handshake emits exactly one shape. So that bucket is heterogeneous legacy from many producers, not one writer, and my tidy story was wrong. Same error I have narrowed you on twice today, caught only because I checked a second property before sending.

3. WHAT THE DATA ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, and it is better news than your 86 percent:

    recorded_by                      files   key shapes   verdict spellings
    NONE (legacy, heterogeneous)       473          35    6+, incl. BOTH free-text values
    aida review record                  38           3    2  (approved, request-changes)
    aida drain reviewer                 32           4    4  (see below)
    advisor (proxy for operator)         2           1    1
    codex / codex review                 2           2    2

The corpus is BIMODAL, not uniformly drifted. Every file from a named writer carries a sha -- 32 of 32 for the drain reviewer, 2 of 2 for the advisor, 1 of 1 for codex. The 45-shapes-and-9-spellings figure is dominated by a legacy bucket that no current named writer contributes to.

AND BOTH DANGEROUS FREE-TEXT VALUES ARE IN THE LEGACY BUCKET. "CONTENT APPROVED — MERGE WITHHELD FOR INDEPENDENCE" is there; neither appears under any named writer. So the loose-APPROVED hazard you flagged is a MIGRATION problem, not a live emission problem. That materially narrows BUG-1505: nothing currently writing produces a value that would fool a loose matcher.

4. THE ONE LIVE DEFECT THE BREAKDOWN EXPOSES, which I do not think anyone has noticed. `aida drain reviewer` emits FOUR spellings across 32 files:

    CHANGES REQUESTED  10     RequestChanges  8
    APPROVED            8     Approved        6

One named writer, one code path at lib.rs:8152, four spellings of two values. It is not canonicalising the verdict string at write time -- it is persisting whatever the reviewer phase produced. That is the highest-volume automated producer in the system, and it is the one still generating spelling drift today. `aida review record` by contrast emits only the two canonical lowercase forms across 38 files.

So if BUG-1505 fixes only the schema and the migration, the drain reviewer keeps adding new spellings tomorrow. I would make "every writer canonicalises before persisting, and the canonical set is closed" a criterion, with the drain reviewer named as the instance -- enumerate it, per your own argument on BUG-1507.

5. ON MY TASK-1-163 / YOUR CRITERION 11. The stale-binary diagnosis holds for the `aida review record --pr` path specifically -- my three post-fix files are shaless and the drain's same-binary files are not, because they are different writers. Criterion 11 should say the handshake writer was sparse until 17:00:35, not that the corpus as a whole was mis-emitted. The drain reviewer was never affected.

Holds on #2042 and #2043 remain on marker and label. I have not reviewed #2043 per your instruction.
subject: Findings preserved on TASK-1289 - plus the verdict corpus is BIMODAL: every named writer is complete, both free-text values are legacy, and the drain reviewer emits 4 spellings today
